topics.topic: Required and permitted trial-case input and expected-output port coverage
questions: Must inputs contain exactly every declared input and no extra names, and, when expected outputs are present, must they contain exactly every declared output or may they be partial?
Must trial inputs contain exactly every input port and no extras, and when expected_outputs is present must it contain exactly every output port or may it assert only a subset?
When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it contain only a subset to be compared?

quotes: add_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown contract version; then RefusedError naming the first name in inputs that is not an input port of the contract version, then the first name in expected_outputs that is not an output port, each taken by name; then checks each input port and, when expected_outputs is given, each output port, in port name order, by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for value ports and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant for file ports, a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type; the first failing check, presence, carriage, schema then size, raises RefusedError naming port and check, and nothing is written. A trial case therefore names exactly the contract's input ports, and expected_outputs is either absent or names exactly every output port: a partial expected_outputs, and an empty object, is given and fails presence at its first missing port; only absence means no expected outputs.
judgement.why: The later notes require exactly every input port and, when expected_outputs is present, exactly every output port.

topics.topic: Unit and truncation basis of masked failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length the number of Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
What unit is used for the disclosed failure_detail length?

quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later notes define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded failure_detail.

topics.topic: Deterministic ordering when flow identity sort keys tie
questions: How is hashing order made deterministic when two edges or constants have the same stated sort key but differ in other facts?
How are edges with identical endpoints but different guards, and constants with the same target but different contents, ordered for hashing and first-failure selection when the stated keys tie?

judgement.why: Tie-breaking within canonical identity ordering is an encoding and deterministic-order contract matter belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Duplicate JSON member detection and canonical_bytes input representation
questions: Are duplicate object member names in configuration or manifest JSON refused, and under which failure, or may the JSON parser select one occurrence?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text that still exposes duplicate object keys, or an already parsed value—and, in the latter case, which operation detects duplicate keys?

judgement.why: JSON parsing, duplicate-member handling and the representation passed to canonicalization are format and contract matters belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Exact sandbox startup probe specification and required coverage
questions: What implementation, inputs, bounds and expected result constitute the probe, and which sandbox properties must it exercise before startup succeeds?
What exact code, inputs, bounds and expected result constitute the probe whose failure prevents the kernel from starting?

quotes: probe_sandbox: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise SandboxUnavailableError naming what is missing when the bubblewrap executable cannot be found, or when one probe execution through execute_function of a minimal implementation with no ports, under bounds equal to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_WALL_TIME_MS, RELEASE_CEILING_MEMORY_BYTES, RELEASE_CEILING_OUTPUT_BYTES and RELEASE_CEILING_PROCESS_COUNT constants, does not end succeeded, naming its outcome.
probe_sandbox: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns None when bubblewrap is present and the probe execution succeeded; it writes no record.
judgement.why: The later notes specify a minimal no-port execution through execute_function, release-ceiling bounds, and succeeded as the required result.

questions: What exact encoding is used for path strings and integers, and are percent-escape hex digits uppercase or lowercase?
What exact textual form is used for integer placeholders, and which characters, UTF-8 encoding and percent-escape casing are used for string placeholders?

judgement.why: The exact textual and percent-encoding rules for path placeholders are encoding contracts belonging to State 6 or later.

May api_base_url contain user information, a path, query, fragment, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how are those components combined with the declared path?

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms and deterministic operation-path joining
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

Which port names and media-type strings are valid in multipart requests, and are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII names or media-type parameters rejected or escaped?

topics.topic: JSON equality semantics for guard comparisons
questions: What definition of JSON equality is used for a guard, especially for numbers and for language-level cases such as boolean true versus integer 1?

topics.topic: Propagation of put_value_bytes refusal from internally computed metadata

topics.topic: Reading immutable manifest content at a named revision
questions: How must bindings read a file at the named revision, and what guarantees that a revision cannot change beneath a running kernel?

topics.topic: Repair-view treatment of pinned implementations that never ran

topics.topic: Sandbox outcome when returned values cannot be canonicalized

topics.topic: Security classification of empty mapped outputs

topics.topic: Source of file fixture bytes in authored trial cases

topics.topic: Startup manifest checks when no operation or proposed ports exist

topics.topic: Validation, storage, spooling order, and publication atomicity of multiple function outputs
questions: In what order are multiple function outputs validated, size-checked, stored and spooled, and are all outputs checked before any file is published?

topics.topic: Whether approval success guarantees an HTTP send
questions: Does a successful approval operation guarantee that an HTTP request was sent, or only that the approval was recorded and the element was reached again?

topics.topic: Whether run resumption guarantees resending service-unreachable elements
